title: What you send, cut into tokens
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers from brain3d/trace.json, films/qkv_data.json, experiments/logs.

blocks.text: Last section, text went in. But a model never sees letters. It sees tokens: pieces of text, each with a number.
blocks.say: Last section, text went in. But a model never sees letters. It sees tokens: pieces of text, each with a number.

blocks.text: Emma's chat is cut into 100 tiles. 72 for the app's instructions, 15 for her question, and 13 for the markers that say who is speaking.
blocks.say: Emma's chat is cut into one hundred tiles. Seventy-two for the app's instructions, fifteen for her question, and thirteen for the markers that say who is speaking.

blocks.text: Common words are one tile each. Manchester is one token, number 19361. Northbridge is two: North, bridge. And a number is cut digit by digit. 5,400 becomes five tokens: five, comma, four, zero, zero.
blocks.say: Common words are one tile each. Manchester is one token, number one nine three six one. Northbridge is two: North, bridge. And a number is cut digit by digit. Five thousand four hundred becomes five tokens: five, comma, four, zero, zero.

blocks.text: Where do the pieces come from? From byte pair encoding. Start with single bytes, then keep merging the pair that appears most often in a huge pile of text. Qwen's tokenizer learned 151,643 pieces this way.
blocks.say: Where do the pieces come from? From byte pair encoding. Start with single bytes, then keep merging the pair that appears most often in a huge pile of text. Qwen's tokenizer learned one hundred and fifty-one thousand, six hundred and forty-three pieces this way.

blocks.text: Add 22 special tokens, like the markers in Emma's chat, and the tokenizer knows 151,665 pieces. The model keeps one row in its table for each.
blocks.say: Add twenty-two special tokens, like the markers in Emma's chat, and the tokenizer knows one hundred and fifty-one thousand, six hundred and sixty-five pieces. The model keeps one row in its table for each.

blocks.text: So: 100 tokens in. That is what Emma's question costs, and exactly what the model reads.
blocks.say: So: one hundred tokens in. That is what Emma's question costs, and exactly what the model reads.
